cost: Add costs only along reached call chains, not across independent tools. Character/CSV scans generally O(bytes); conservative repeated wiki/cleanup scans O(bytes^2); OCR DP O((n+1)(m+1)) memory/time, word alignment O((N+1)(M+1)*(L+1)^2); Kaggle 36 candidates/row, at most twelve retained rules and thirteen candidate-building iterations and dense neighbor dedup O(N^3) per reconstruction; indexed pages decode streams repeatedly per title. Network/process/corpus throughput unmeasured.
description: Tagged union of seven independent CLI relations: Gutenberg CSV selection/fetch; Kaggle CSV feature/rule/group prediction; OCR normalization/correction/alignment/masking; school text cleanup/sentence/address export; Wiktionary count, idiom emission and exact-page lookup. Real in-file joins include csv_rows -> select/death_years gates, feats -> learn/predict_list, Channel -> Corrector -> token, letter_stream -> align, usfm_verses -> verse_sentences, EnAgg.page -> en_line/flush, labels/regions/plain -> emit, and read_stream -> find_page.

Real in-file joins include csv_rows -> select/death_years gates, feats -> learn/predict_list, Channel -> Corrector -> token, letter_stream -> align, usfm_verses -> verse_sentences, EnAgg.page -> en_line/flush, labels/regions/plain -> emit, and read_stream -> find_page.

Actual joins are within each tool; no cross-tool Rust caller is invented. A possible explicit artifact adapter maps Gutenberg fetched pg-id text into school book_paragraphs -> sentences, losing headers/underscores/short fragments. OCR output is Unicode line text and is not directly a school address TSV. Wiktionary page raw wikitext can be supplied to count/emit helpers only with edition/title/namespace context; these tools do not call one another. Tests exercise actual local helper joins only; cross-tool adapters remain source-derived.
inverse: For each tagged relation, excluded effects follow its gates: no later matching Gutenberg group, no transitive Kaggle group edge, no short OCR word change, no cut-only two-word school sentence, no translation-subpage En section, no unlabeled single-word idiom row, no mismatched exact XML page. These are scoped source-derived exclusions; independent tool complements are not unioned into an invented pipeline.

Recover compatible antecedents per tag: catalog rows satisfying first-match/date predicates; passenger feature/group-label fibers; pointed texts sharing corrected skeleton; markup texts sharing emitted sentence; page multisets sharing counts; wikitext sharing gloss; XML sharing Page fields. Preserve multiple possibilities and hidden rejected inputs; no unique corpus reconstruction.
limitations: Seven file roots and seven scoped fragments are partial source models, not full semantics.
Wiktionary count export parser and report writes, page index/decompression, Gutenberg selection/fetch effects, OCR subprocesses and school output workflows remain unexecuted.
Wikt-idioms English slice only checks first following heading; Ukrainian report tie ordering incomplete. Empty Kaggle CV NaN and permissive malformed inputs retained.
No cross-tool runtime adapter claim, corpus accuracy, universal proof, speedup or percent surrogate.
state: Tagged routing prevents treating similarly named text artifacts as interchangeable. UTF-8 bytes, chars, row indices, passenger ids and verse coordinates are separate spaces. Repeated pure fixtures match across profiles. Lossy normalizers and aggregated counts do not uniquely recover input. File/output effects are sequential and lack rollback.
